text: {"claims": [{"id": "c1", "evidence": [{"sid": "P5.S3", "rel": "entails"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P5.S3 directly states all checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and the automatic mechanism are PASSIVE, matching the claim."}, {"id": "c2", "evidence": [], "check": null, "reasoning": "P5.S4 gives a necessary condition for FULL/RESTART, not a sufficient one; it does not entail that every sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() call produces FULL/RESTART."}, {"id": "c3", "evidence": [{"sid": "P5.S2", "rel": "refutes"}, {"sid": "P7.S1", "rel": "refutes"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P5.S2 says PASSIVE may not complete with concurrent readers or writers; P7.S1 requires no other connections, not merely no writers, for completion/reset."}, {"id": "c5", "evidence": [], "check": null, "reasoning": "P7.S1 states only a necessary condition for reset; it does not entail that an unused WAL is always reset by a checkpoint."}, {"id": "c8", "evidence": [{"sid": "P2.S0", "rel": "refutes"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P2.S0 says long-running read transactions can prevent checkpointer progress, contradicting the claim that readers never delay the automatic checkpoint."}]}
